CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction and pre-operative clearance for right knee replacement surgery.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Nicole Miller is a 76-year-old female presenting for follow-up of chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction. She had an exacerbation of CHF earlier in the spring with increasing dyspnea. At that time, her furosemide was changed to torsemide 20 mg daily and her lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily. She reports good compliance with medications. She has lost approximately 3 to 3.5 pounds since last visit in April. She notes improved urinary urgency and decreased dyspnea on the current regimen. She had bilateral leg cramps a few days ago which resolved after drinking pickle juice. She denies ongoing leg or finger cramps. She is scheduled for right knee replacement surgery on June 24th at East Metro. She is interested in having a colonoscopy performed within the next 30 days due to potential change in insurance coverage. She reports good appetite and denies orthopnea or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports recent resolution of heartburn after taking Prilosec for two weeks in January and stopping a previous antacid medication. No current heartburn complaints. She is using the bathroom appropriately. She continues iron supplementation. She denies leg swelling, chest pain, palpitations, or syncope. Lungs sound clear on examination with non-labored breathing.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction
2. History of anemia
3. Diabetes mellitus
4. Heartburn (recently resolved)
5. Right knee pathology requiring surgical replacement

MEDICATIONS
1. Torsemide 20 mg daily
2. Lisinopril 10 mg daily
3. Clopidogrel (to be discontinued one week prior to surgery)
4. Iron supplement
5. Prilosec (recently discontinued)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in conversation.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of colon cancer.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is married. She is organized with her medications, keeping notes on her phone and reminders taped to her bed. She will be undergoing elective right knee replacement surgery at East Metro on June 24th. She has Medicare and private insurance.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles, good air movement
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm
Blood Pressure: Good control
Overall: Well-appearing, non-labored breathing

RESULTS
Laboratory values from today's visit:
- Hemoglobin: Normal, good control of anemia
- Potassium: 3.9 (stable on torsemide)
- Creatinine: 0.7 (appropriate kidney function)
- BUN: 23 (slightly elevated, may suggest mild dehydration, not concerning)
- Magnesium: 1.7 (normal)
- Blood glucose: 169 (non-fasting)
- A1C: 5.5 in March (last check)
- BNP: Pending (was 3,000 in March, 6,000 in April prior to medication adjustment)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Chronic Congestive Heart Failure with mixed presentation: Patient had exacerbation of CHF earlier in spring with dyspnea. Changed from furosemide to torsemide with good symptomatic improvement. Weight loss of 3-3.5 pounds, breathing non-labored. Labs show appropriate creatinine. Continue current regimen. Repeat EKG today. Recommend magnesium supplementation twice daily to maintain levels around 2.0 for cardiac stability.

2. Pre-operative examination: Patient scheduled for right knee replacement on June 24th. Discontinue clopidogrel one week before surgery. Complete pre-operative check within two weeks of surgery (first or second week of June). May repeat EKG before surgery today. No chest X-rays needed (recent study available). No additional blood work needed at this time. Patient tolerating current medications well for pre-operative period.

3. Screening Colonoscopy: Patient is overdue for screening colonoscopy. Referral placed to complete procedure within 30 days prior to change in insurance coverage. Colonoscopy will not delay knee surgery. Options include Dr. Martin at County Surgical Services or Valley Medical at Springfield. If results indicate 10-year interval, patient will be clear for future screening.

4. Diabetes mellitus: A1C was 5.1 on last check, no further A1C today. May repeat A1C prior to surgery next month.
